title: Identifying Molecules with Mass Spec Skills for Antigravity
gist: Google DeepMind launched Mass Spec Skills for Google Antigravity, an agent that chains open-source mass spectrometry tools and public databases with Gemini reasoning to turn tandem mass spectra into verified molecular structures, attacking the ~95% of spectra that library search leaves unannotated. On a 100-compound benchmark, skills lifted exact-match accuracy from <4% (no tools) to ~97%, let the lightweight Gemini 3.8 Flash match frontier models, and cut tokens per attempt by up to ~4x.

insights.claim: Even after a decade of expanding reference libraries, spectral library searches annotate only about 5% of measured tandem mass spectra on average (10% for human samples), leaving the rest as the 'dark matter' of mass spectrometry.
insights.speaker: DeepMind Blog
insights.so_what: A ~90-95% unannotated data pool is the addressable gap for AI-driven metabolomics, drug-discovery and diagnostics tooling.
insights.quote: spectral searches annotate on average only about 5% of measured spectra, and 10% for human samples
insights.locator: Yet even after a decade of expanding reference libraries

insights.claim: Many unannotated mass-spec signals come from molecules already listed in public chemical databases but whose reference spectra were never recorded, so identification requires inferring structure directly from fragment ions rather than library matching.
insights.speaker: DeepMind Blog
insights.so_what: Tools that bridge chemical databases and de novo fragment interpretation unlock value from existing data without new measurements.
insights.locator: Many of the molecules producing these unannotated signals

insights.claim: The expert workflow for identifying molecules from MS/MS spectra (library check, formula determination, candidate retrieval, fragment testing) uses openly available tools but is too slow per spectrum for studies that produce thousands of spectra, so manual analysis cannot keep up.
insights.speaker: DeepMind Blog
insights.so_what: Labor-bound, tool-rich expert workflows are prime targets for agentic automation; throughput rather than tool availability is the constraint.
insights.quote: manual analysis cannot keep up, leaving most of these signals unannotated
insights.locator: The tools for each step exist and are openly available

insights.claim: Google DeepMind's Mass Spec Skills for Google Antigravity pair Gemini's chemical reasoning with the ability to run established mass spectrometry tools and query public chemical databases, producing a proposed structure and an auditable evidence report for chemist review.
insights.speaker: DeepMind Blog
insights.so_what: Signals Google's strategy of vertical scientific 'skills' plugins on its agent IDE as a wedge into lab and pharma R&D workflows.
insights.locator: Today, we are sharing Mass Spec Skills

insights.claim: DeepMind argues a language model cannot identify molecules from mass spectra on its own because the task requires precise mass calculations, searches across databases of millions of compounds and bond-breaking simulations, so LLM reasoning must be paired with dedicated chemistry tools.
insights.speaker: DeepMind Blog
insights.so_what: Supports the thesis that domain tool integration, not raw model scale, is the moat for scientific AI agents.
insights.quote: A language model cannot do this on its own, since matching fragments to a structure takes precise mass calculations
insights.locator: A language model cannot do this on its own

insights.claim: The Mass Spec Skills wrap community open-source tools including matchms, GNPS and MoNA library search, SIRIUS fragmentation trees, MAGMa, MetFrag and RDKit, chaining them automatically from a plain-language prompt so non-computational scientists can use them.
insights.speaker: DeepMind Blog
insights.so_what: Agent layers commoditize access to open-source scientific software; value accrues to the orchestrator platform rather than the individual tools.
insights.locator: Researchers can describe their task and any instrument-specific tolerances

insights.claim: Spectral coverage scores alone cannot separate isomers: in DeepMind's worked example the true molecule and two rejected non-urea isomers all explained the same 97.7% of summed fragment intensity, and only checking diagnostic neutral losses and bond connectivity, as a chemist would, identified the correct structure.
insights.speaker: DeepMind Blog
insights.so_what: Shows where LLM reasoning adds value on top of deterministic scoring tools: tie-breaking via mechanistic chemistry.
insights.quote: Spectral coverage measures how much peak intensity a candidate matches by mass alone
insights.locator: Spectral coverage measures how much peak intensity

insights.claim: In an end-to-end negative-mode example with library lookup disabled, the agent filtered 1,761 raw peaks to 19, used SIRIUS to find formula C20H21ClN6O at -1.5 ppm error, scored all 845 PubChem isomers, narrowed to five urea regioisomers and singled out the true molecule (CID 137835447).
insights.speaker: DeepMind Blog
insights.so_what: Demonstrates the agent can handle harder negative-ion spectra, where reference libraries are thin, extending addressable data.
insights.locator: From raw spectrum to structure end-to-end

insights.claim: On 100 Enamine REAL compounds from MoNA, Antigravity with no internet or skills scored below 4% exact-match accuracy across Gemini 3.8 Flash, Gemini 4 Argon and Gemini 4 Carbon, showing frontier models cannot deduce structures from peak lists alone.
insights.speaker: DeepMind Blog
insights.so_what: Raw model capability is not yet a substitute for tooling in analytical chemistry; discount claims of LLMs 'doing science' unaided.
insights.quote: accuracy remained below 4% across all three models
insights.locator: With no internet access or skills, accuracy remained below 4%

insights.claim: Giving the agent internet access alone was insufficient: improvised search scripts were brittle around precursor windows, adducts and noisy peaks, causing frontier models to miss a quarter to a third of spectra and the lightweight model to miss more than three-quarters.
insights.speaker: DeepMind Blog
insights.so_what: Generic web/tool access is not a reliable path to domain performance; curated, validated skills are what close the gap.
insights.quote: custom search scripts written from scratch proved brittle around precursor windows, adducts, and noisy peaks
insights.locator: Giving the agent limited internet access

insights.claim: With Mass Spec Skills added, all three Gemini models identified and verified the exact molecule in around 97% of attempts, with the lightweight Gemini 3.8 Flash matching frontier-model accuracy.
insights.speaker: DeepMind Blog
insights.so_what: Well-built skills let cheap small models match frontier accuracy, pressuring inference pricing and favoring tooling/workflow ownership over model size.
insights.quote: with the lightweight model matching the frontier models' accuracy
insights.locator: With the Mass Spec Skills added, all three models

insights.claim: Mass Spec Skills cut generated tokens per attempt across every model, by nearly four times on Gemini 3.8 Flash, by half on Gemini 4 Argon and by nearly a fifth on Gemini 4 Carbon, because the agent calls validated ready-made skills instead of improvising API queries and debugging scripts.
insights.speaker: DeepMind Blog
insights.so_what: Domain skills lower compute cost per task, improving unit economics of agentic science and reducing per-query token revenue for model providers.
insights.quote: by nearly four times on Flash, by half on Argon, and by nearly a fifth on Carbon
insights.locator: Skills also cut token cost and effort

insights.claim: A University of Pretoria researcher reports Antigravity with Mass Spec Skills achieved over 90% accuracy in most of their evaluations predicting complex structures, and could accelerate identification of bioactive compounds from plant extracts for natural-product drug discovery.
insights.speaker: DeepMind Blog
insights.so_what: Early academic validation in natural-product drug discovery; watch for pharma/biotech adoption of agentic metabolomics.
insights.quote: Their remarkable accuracy in predicting even highly complex molecular structures (>90% in most of our evaluations)
insights.locator: Antigravity and the Mass Spec Skills have the potential to transform

insights.claim: A Technical University of Denmark professor says agentic de novo structure prediction reduces MS/MS analysis that previously took days or months of analysis and literature review to a matter of hours, enabling faster prioritization of metabolite classes for drug discovery.
insights.speaker: DeepMind Blog
insights.so_what: Order-of-magnitude cycle-time compression in compound annotation could shorten early-stage discovery timelines.
insights.quote: reduces a complicated process - one that previously required days or months of analysis and literature review - to a matter of hours
insights.locator: Antigravity and Mass Spec Skills takes a big leap forward

insights.claim: A Princeton University (Rabinowitz Lab) specialist describes Gemini plus the agent plus Mass Spec Skills as a 'golden triad' that feels like hiring an in silico team and makes advanced analysis accessible to users without coding or domain-tool expertise.
insights.speaker: DeepMind Blog
insights.so_what: Framing AI agents as substitutes for specialist staff points to labor-substitution value propositions in lab software.
insights.quote: feels just like hiring an in silico team
insights.locator: I’ve been testing Antigravity equipped with Mass Spec skills

insights.claim: Google is offering 10,000 scientists the highest Google Antigravity usage tier free for 6 months and makes Mass Spec Skills available to Enterprise users via Google Cloud credentials, an aggressive land-grab for scientific users.
insights.speaker: DeepMind Blog
insights.so_what: Subsidized adoption plus Google Cloud enterprise distribution positions Google against rival AI-for-science platforms; watch conversion to paid cloud usage.
insights.quote: we’re offering 10,000 scientists the highest usage tier in Google Antigravity free of charge for 6 months
insights.locator: To further advance the pace of research

insights.claim: LC-MS/MS spectra fundamentally cannot distinguish mirror-image molecules and some closely related isomers, which require other measurements such as chromatographic retention time, ion mobility or NMR.
insights.speaker: DeepMind Blog
insights.so_what: AI agents on mass-spec data do not eliminate demand for orthogonal analytical instruments; multimodal integration is the next frontier.
insights.quote: telling them apart requires other measurements, such as chromatographic retention time, ion mobility, or NMR
insights.locator: However, there are some questions that cannot be answered

insights.claim: For genuinely new molecules, including many natural products absent from all databases, Antigravity cannot retrieve or confirm a structure itself but provides a predicted formula, peak assignments and annotation table as a starting point for chemists.
insights.speaker: DeepMind Blog
insights.so_what: The agent is a chemist-in-the-loop accelerator, not a replacement, for the highest-value novel-compound discovery.
insights.locator: Genuinely new molecules, including many natural products

insights.claim: DeepMind sees scaling automated spectral interpretation from single spectra to full metabolomics studies as the path to identifying far more unknown small molecules across human health, environmental science and natural-product discovery.
insights.speaker: DeepMind Blog
insights.so_what: Points to a broader AI-for-metabolomics market spanning diagnostics, environmental monitoring and drug discovery.

source_meta.author: Robert Brunck, Stefan Ganscha, Swaroop Guntupalli, Dariusz Lasecki, Gabriella Marfani, Jack Mason, Hussain Masoom, Rose
